title: Using AI as a Development Assistant
description: Build AI literacy through task briefs, context selection, prompting, constrained agent permissions, evidence, and review.

lessons.title: What coding AI can and cannot do
lessons.principle: Models predict useful code and explanations from context, but may fabricate APIs, miss requirements, and overlook risks.
lessons.practice: Use AI to explore, explain, draft, test, and review while keeping source code and runtime behavior authoritative.

lessons.title: Calibrate model confidence
lessons.principle: Fluent output is not a measurement of correctness or compatibility.
lessons.practice: Ask for exact references to repository files or docs and verify them rather than trusting stated certainty.

lessons.title: Well-formed task briefs
lessons.principle: A strong request names the goal, context, constraints, expected output, and definition of done.
lessons.practice: Give AI the runtime, relevant files, in-scope change, and validation commands.

lessons.title: Compare weak and strong prompts
lessons.principle: 'Make an app' leaves hundreds of uncontrolled assumptions.
lessons.practice: Specify 'Add task creation to this static app; preserve storage format; reject blanks; add a test' instead.

lessons.title: Selecting repository context
lessons.principle: Too much irrelevant context hides crucial constraints; missing context causes incorrect assumptions.
lessons.practice: Provide a repository map, the affected modules, failing test, and local project rules.

lessons.title: Avoid stale context
lessons.principle: An agent may reason from an old branch or a prior file snapshot.
lessons.practice: Ask it to inspect the current default branch or active PR head before proposing edits.

lessons.title: Prompt decomposition
lessons.principle: Complex work becomes reviewable when discovery, design, implementation, and verification are separate stages.
lessons.practice: Ask first for unknowns and a bounded plan, then authorize an isolated implementation step.

lessons.title: Manage task boundaries
lessons.principle: A single prompt that mixes redesign, dependencies, migrations, and deployment raises regression risk.
lessons.practice: Create separate acceptance checks and file scopes for independent steps.

lessons.title: Good AI-generated explanations
lessons.principle: A useful explanation connects each change to user behavior, data flow, and specific code paths.
lessons.practice: Ask AI to explain the data path in simple terms after it writes a function.

lessons.title: Learn without outsourcing understanding
lessons.principle: Accepting a patch that no human can debug creates long-term maintenance risk.
lessons.practice: Explain one generated function back in your own words and change a test without the model.

lessons.title: Code editing with checkpoints
lessons.principle: Small patches and focused diffs are easier to verify and reverse than sweeping rewrites.
lessons.practice: Request one coherent behavior change, inspect the diff, and commit only after checks.

lessons.title: Preserve unmodified behavior
lessons.principle: AI can accidentally drop error handling, accessibility, or event listeners during a rewrite.
lessons.practice: Inspect before-and-after behavior for every touched user journey.

lessons.title: Tool access and agent permissions
lessons.principle: Tool-enabled agents can run commands and change remote systems, making permission scope material.
lessons.practice: Grant the minimum repository, network, deployment, and credential access needed.

lessons.title: Distinguish read from write
lessons.principle: An agent asked to investigate does not require permission to merge, delete, deploy, or mutate user data.
lessons.practice: Keep destructive and production actions behind explicit human-approved gates.

lessons.title: Hallucinations and documentation checks
lessons.principle: Generated package names, APIs, arguments, URLs, and version claims may not exist or may be obsolete.
lessons.practice: Check an unfamiliar API in official version-matched documentation.

lessons.title: Test the proposed method
lessons.principle: A model's sample can compile while relying on wrong runtime assumptions.
lessons.practice: Run a minimal reproduction with representative values before integrating unfamiliar code.

lessons.title: AI review as a second opinion
lessons.principle: Independent review helps surface defects but may share the same blind spots as generation.
lessons.practice: Ask a reviewer to look for correctness, risks, missing cases, and scope drift using the actual diff.

lessons.title: Use adversarial checks
lessons.principle: Request counterexamples rather than only reasons why the change is good.
lessons.practice: Ask what input, permission combination, or failure mode would break the new behavior, then test it.

lessons.title: Knowing when to stop
lessons.principle: Repeated prompting without new evidence can degrade a correct implementation.
lessons.practice: Use acceptance criteria and evidence as the stop condition.

lessons.title: Keep residual-risk notes
lessons.principle: No reasonable test suite proves the absence of all defects; known limits should remain explicit.
lessons.practice: Summarize validated behavior, untested environments, remaining risks, and the recovery plan.

codeExamples.snippet:
Goal: reject blank task titles
Context: static JS app; localStorage data shape unchanged
Scope: task-form.js and its tests only
Acceptance: trimmed blanks rejected; valid titles saved
Validation: npm test; inspect final diff

Review only the current diff.
Find: behavioral regressions, unhandled errors,
unsafe data flow, and missing edge cases.
For each finding: path, evidence, impact, test.
Do not edit or merge without authorization.
